1.overview: As David grows old, Adonijah claims the throne and gathers supporters, while Nathan and Bathsheba urge David to confirm Solomon as his successor. David orders Solomon’s anointing at Gihon, and when Adonijah’s feast collapses, Solomon spares him on condition of good conduct and sends him home.

sections.heading: Nathan and Bathsheba Appeal to David

2.overview: As David nears death, he charges Solomon to keep the LORD’s commands and gives instructions concerning Joab, Barzillai’s family, and Shimei; David dies, and Solomon’s kingdom is established. Solomon executes Adonijah and Joab, removes Abiathar from the priesthood, appoints Benaiah and Zadok, and has Shimei killed after he breaks the king’s restriction.

3.overview: Solomon forms an alliance with Pharaoh through marriage and worships at Gibeon, where the LORD offers him whatever he asks; Solomon requests discernment to govern Israel, and God grants him wisdom, riches, and honor. In Jerusalem, Solomon resolves a dispute between two women over a living child, and Israel recognizes his God-given wisdom in administering justice.

4.overview: Solomon rules Israel with a named group of chief officials and twelve regional governors who provide food for the king and his household. Judah and Israel prosper under his wide-ranging rule, while God gives Solomon exceptional wisdom, expressed in his proverbs, songs, and teaching, which draws visitors from many nations.

5.overview: Hiram of Tyre contacts Solomon, who explains that the LORD has given him peace to build the temple and asks for cedar from Lebanon; Hiram agrees to supply timber in exchange for food, and the two kings make a treaty. Solomon organizes Israelite laborers, porters, stonecutters, and foremen to quarry and prepare stone and timber for the temple.

sections.heading: Labor and Materials for the Temple

6.overview: Solomon builds the temple in Jerusalem, with its dimensions, side chambers, cedar interior, gold overlay, inner sanctuary, and carved furnishings. The LORD promises to dwell among Israel if Solomon keeps the commandments, and the temple is completed in the eleventh year of Solomon’s reign, seven years after construction begins.

sections.heading: The LORD’s promise and temple interior

7.overview: Solomon completes his palace complex, including the House of the Forest of Lebanon, the Hall of Justice, and residences for himself and Pharaoh’s daughter. Huram of Tyre makes the temple’s bronze pillars, Sea, stands, basins, and utensils, and Solomon completes the gold furnishings and places David’s dedicated treasures in the temple storehouses.

8.overview: Solomon brings the ark into the temple, where the LORD’s glory fills the house, and blesses Israel by recounting how the temple fulfills the promise to David. He prays for the LORD to hear and forgive Israel and foreigners who pray toward the temple, then blesses the people as they dedicate the house with sacrifices and celebrate before returning home.

sections.heading: Solomon Recalls the Promise to David

9.overview: The LORD appears to Solomon, consecrates the temple, and promises an enduring throne if Solomon and his descendants obey, while warning that apostasy will bring Israel’s expulsion and the temple’s ruin. Solomon gives Hiram towns in Galilee, undertakes building projects with forced labor, completes temple worship, and sends a fleet with Hiram’s sailors to Ophir for gold.

10.overview: The queen of Sheba visits Solomon in Jerusalem, tests his wisdom, praises the LORD for establishing him as king, and exchanges gifts with him before returning home. The chapter describes Solomon’s annual income, royal wealth and splendor, international reputation for wisdom, and trade in horses and chariots.

sections.heading: The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon

11.overview: Solomon turns to the gods of his foreign wives, and the LORD declares that the kingdom will be divided, leaving one tribe to David’s line. The chapter recounts the adversaries Hadad and Rezon, Ahijah’s promise of ten tribes to Jeroboam, Jeroboam’s flight to Egypt, and Solomon’s death and succession by Rehoboam.

sections.heading: Solomon’s Idolatry and the Kingdom’s Judgment

12.overview: At Shechem, Rehoboam rejects the elders’ counsel and answers Israel’s request for lighter service with threats, prompting the northern tribes to make Jeroboam king and dividing the kingdom. Rehoboam abandons a planned attack after Shemaiah relays the LORD’s command, while Jeroboam establishes rival worship centers at Bethel and Dan and institutes a feast and priesthood outside Jerusalem.

13.overview: A man of God from Judah proclaims the future judgment of Bethel’s altar, and the altar splits as Jeroboam’s withered hand is restored; the man then refuses the king’s hospitality and leaves by another road. An old prophet deceives him into returning to eat, then delivers the LORD’s judgment, and the man dies on the road and is buried in the prophet’s tomb; Jeroboam continues appointing priests for the high places.

sections.heading: The Man of God’s Death and Burial

14.overview: Jeroboam’s disguised wife visits Ahijah at Shiloh, where the prophet announces the death of Abijah and judgment on Jeroboam’s house and Israel; Abijah dies, and Jeroboam is succeeded by Nadab. Rehoboam reigns in Judah, where idolatrous practices spread and Shishak of Egypt plunders Jerusalem’s temple and palace before Rehoboam is succeeded by Abijam.

15.overview: Abijam rules Judah in sin while the LORD preserves David’s line, and Asa succeeds him, removes idols, and uses an alliance with Aram to counter Baasha’s pressure on Judah. In Israel, Baasha kills Nadab, destroys Jeroboam’s household in fulfillment of the LORD’s word, and rules in Jeroboam’s sinful pattern.

sections.heading: Asa’s Reign and Conflict with Baasha

16.overview: Jehu announces judgment on Baasha’s house, and after Baasha and Elah die, Zimri kills Baasha’s household before Israel’s army backs Omri and Zimri dies. Omri defeats Tibni, establishes Samaria, and is succeeded by Ahab, whose Baal worship intensifies Israel’s idolatry as Hiel rebuilds Jericho at the cost of his sons, fulfilling Joshua’s word.

sections.heading: Omri Becomes King and Builds Samaria

17.overview: Elijah announces to Ahab that Israel will have no dew or rain except at his word, then lives beside the Brook of Cherith, where ravens bring him food until the brook dries up. At the LORD’s command, he goes to Zarephath, where a widow’s flour and oil remain sufficient through the drought, and he restores her son to life.

sections.heading: Elijah at the Brook of Cherith

18.overview: In the third year of the drought, Elijah meets Ahab and challenges the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, where the LORD answers Elijah’s sacrifice with fire and the people acknowledge the LORD as God. Elijah orders the prophets of Baal seized, announces rain, and, after a small cloud appears over the sea, runs ahead of Ahab to Jezreel as the storm breaks.

19.overview: After Jezebel threatens him, Elijah flees to the wilderness, where an angel feeds him before he travels to Horeb. There the LORD meets Elijah in a still, small voice, sends him to anoint Hazael and Jehu and appoint Elisha, and reveals that seven thousand Israelites remain faithful to God; Elijah then calls Elisha to follow him.

20.overview: Ben-hadad of Aram besieges Samaria and demands Ahab’s wealth and family, but Israel defeats the Arameans after a prophet promises victory. After a second victory at Aphek, Ahab makes a treaty with Ben-hadad, and a prophet declares that Ahab and Israel will bear the consequences of sparing him.

sections.heading: Victory at Aphek and Ahab’s treaty

21.overview: Ahab covets Naboth’s vineyard, and Jezebel arranges Naboth’s execution so Ahab can take possession of it. Elijah announces the LORD’s judgment on Ahab’s house and Jezebel, but Ahab’s humility leads the LORD to defer the calamity until his son’s days.

22.overview: After three years of peace, Ahab and Jehoshaphat plan to retake Ramoth-gilead, but Micaiah prophesies Ahab’s defeat and is imprisoned. Ahab dies in battle as Micaiah foretells, and the chapter records the reigns of Jehoshaphat, Ahaziah, and Ahab’s successor.

sections.heading: The reigns of Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah
